messages.body_plain:
Hi all.

I am doing a project in which I do a DIF analysis of a set of 9 items with 4 response categories and 8000 respondents. I have 4 groups with each 2000 respondents. I use a graded response model, and my multigroup analysis can run with the 4 groups.
However when I do a DIF analysis with sequential drop with the 4 groups I get following error-code: "Error in dimnames(x) <- dn :
length of 'dimnames' [1] not equal to array extent
"
If I run a DIF with just two groups, no problems at all.
When looking at the error it seems something in my inputs or coding, when I do it.

I have attach my dataset and some R coding of what I do, and then get the error-code.

I hope somebody can help.

Best regards,
Morten Rasmus Puck

messages.subject: Using mirt to combine multiple datasets with common items for further analysis
messages.subject_clean: Using mirt to combine multiple datasets with common items for further analysis
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am working on a project where the goal is to examine the factor structure of ratings made on items that come from multiple measures of the same construct. I would like to use the mirt package to combine the datasets into one, so that I can factor analyze this dataset in a future step.

I have several datasets and they are each on the small end (~200 participants). There is no overlap in participants, but there is an overlap in items across the datasets. One complication is that the response format differs in some datasets, although the items are the same (e.g., on a scale of 1-7 vs. 1-5). Here are some simplified examples of the datasets.

Dataset 1:

ID PL1 PL2 PL3 PL4 PL5 CL1 CL2 CL3 CL4 CL5 FL1 FL2 FL3 FL4 FL5

1     X     X     X     X     X                                          X     X     X     X     X

2     X     X     X     X     X                                          X     X     X     X     X

3     X     X     X     X     X                                          X     X     X     X     X

Dataset 2:

ID PL1 PL2 PL3 PL4 PL5 CL1 CL2 CL3 CL4 CL5 FL1 FL2 FL3 FL4 FL5

1                                          X     X     X     X     X     X     X     X     X     X

2                                          X     X     X     X     X     X     X     X     X     X

3                                          X     X     X     X     X     X     X     X     X     X

Dataset 3:

ID PL1 PL2 PL3 PL4 PL5 CL1 CL2 CL3 CL4 CL5 FL1 FL2 FL3 FL4 FL5

1     X     X     X     X     X      X     X     X     X    X

2     X     X     X     X     X      X     X     X     X     X

3     X     X     X     X     X      X     X     X     X     X

I was thinking of using a concurrent common-item linking procedure with the hopes of creating a single dataset that I could then factor analyze. Basically, I would like to combine the datasets into one so that it looks like this:

Combined dataset:

ID PL1 PL2 PL3 PL4 PL5 CL1 CL2 CL3 CL4 CL5 FL1 FL2 FL3 FL4 FL5

1     X     X     X     X     X                                          X     X     X     X     X

2     X     X     X     X     X                                          X     X     X     X     X

3     X     X     X     X     X                                          X     X     X     X     X

4                                          X     X     X     X     X     X     X     X     X     X

5                                          X     X     X     X     X     X     X     X     X     X

6                                          X     X     X     X     X     X     X     X     X     X

7     X     X     X     X     X      X     X     X     X    X

8     X     X     X     X     X      X     X     X     X     X

9     X     X     X     X     X      X     X     X     X     X

However, although I have used IRT methods and linking before using mirt, I have never done it in this context (e.g., I've combined different datasets that have all items in common, and in another project, linked two different measures of a construct using external common items to examine theta values longitudinally). Any advice and/or references would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks!

Joanne

messages.subject: Anchoring items manually vs. using multipleGroup vs. linking scores via plink
messages.subject_clean: Anchoring items manually vs. using multipleGroup vs. linking scores via plink
messages.body_plain:
Hi Phil
First, thanks for the amazing package!

I have data on a language test with four items. Test was administered to finnish and swedish kids separately. I've identified two of the items as anchors in order to make the group scores comparable to each other. I seem to have three alternative approaches to score the response patterns that all lead to different score means between the groups.

1. Manually separate unique items and estimate using single-group mirt
2. Use multipleGroup for estimation
3. Estimate models completely separately and use plink package to scale parameters.

Why do the first two options lead to different results? I would greatly appreciate any insights or guidance on choosing the best alternative. Below is a reprex of what I'm trying to do using the first two methods:

# Load the necessary libraries
library(mirt)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# Use the built-in Science dataset
data(Science)

# Split the dataset into two groups
group <- rep(c("Group1", "Group2"), each = 196)

# Estimate IRT model jointly, using two items as anchoring items between groups
mod_multi <- multipleGroup(Science, group = groups,
                           itemtype = "graded",
                           invariance = c("Comfort", "Work", "free_mean", "free_var"),
                           SE = T)

# Estimate IRT model jointly, manually separating non-common items for each group
Science <- cbind(group, Science) %>% mutate(id = 1:392)
Science <- Science %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = c(Future, Benefit)) %>%
  select(-id)

# Joint IRT model
mod_joint <- mirt(Science, itemtype = "graded", SE = T)

# Compare group means
Science %>%
  mutate(fs_multi = fscores(mod_multi),
         fs_joint = fscores(mod_joint),
         group = group) %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  summarise_all(mean, na.rm = T)

messages.subject: understanding latent mean differences
messages.body_plain:
Hi Phil,

Is there any way to find out if the latent mean differences between groups are significant or not? It is possible to get that information in lavaan but I'm not sure how to get that information in mirt. I used coef() to get the latent mean calculations.

This is my code.

mod_configural <- multipleGroup(items_reordered2, model = mirtmodel, group = group)

mod_metric <- multipleGroup(items_reordered2, model = mirtmodel, group = group, invariance=c('slopes')) #equal slopes

#equal intercepts, free variance and means
mod_scalar2 <- multipleGroup(items_reordered2, model = mirtmodel, group = group,
                             invariance=c('slopes', 'intercepts', 'free_var','free_means'))

coef(mod_scalar2, simplify=TRUE)

# compared all at once (in order of most constrained to least)
anova(mod_scalar2,mod_metric, mod_configural)

Is there something equivalent to lavTestScore() in mirt? I want to find out which items should be freely estimated between groups.

                                   AIC          SABIC          HQ              BIC          logLik             X2     df     p
mod_scalar2    31460.96   31597.68   31632.60   31905.69.  -15633.48
mod_metric     31442.48.  31666.59    31723.83   32171.46  -15562.24  142.48   62     0
mod_configural 31458.31 31706.38    31769.74  32265.23   -15553.15   18.172 17 0.378

Thank you,
Aiden

messages.subject: mirt d vs. b location parameters
messages.subject_clean: mirt d vs. b location parameters
messages.body_plain:
I'm sorry if this question was previously asked and answered.

I am working with a graded response model.  Depending on which code I use (see below) the output provides "d" estimates or "b" estimates which are not identical.

model1 <- mirt(dat [ , 1:8], itemtype = "graded", SE = TRUE).
The above produces the slope (a) parameter and two d location parameters, with confidence intervals for all.

vs.

model1 <- (mirt(dat, 1, verbose = FALSE, itemtype = "graded", SE = TRUE)

IRT_parms <- coef(model1, IRTparms = TRUE, simplify = TRUE)

IRT_parms$items

The above produces b estimates which are identical to when I use the ltm package.

So, my questions are as follows:  what are the d estimates, and how are they used?  Second, the printout of d estimates was accompanied by confidence intervals, which is very helpful.  How do I obtain either confidence intervals or standard errors of b estimates?  Is the delta method the only way to do so?  If that is the case, can someone provide a clear, step-by-step example of how to use the delta method?  I'm still relatively new to R.

Thanks so much,

Robert
